notes: TBox subject insert; every derived query is fol (agreement with the subject 'I', counting forms, closed lists). Q2 and Q3 are determinate 'no' since 2026-10-31 (FINDINGS A1), so the record has no worlds.
edit: FrenstleVerb ⊑ EnglishVerb and has_inflection some FirstPersonSingularOnlyForm

queries.not_checked: fol: compares the verb's form after 'I' and after 'you'
fol: agreement of an 'I'-only form with the subject 'they'
fol (closed world): 'the only verb form' over a closed list

fol.notes: Verbs are an uninterpreted sort, persons an enumeration; form(v, p) is the present-tense form after subject p (local). present_forms counts the different forms among the 'I', 'you' and 'he' forms ('they' takes the plain form, as 'you'). The edit states the three forms and the group's existence; 'newly coined' keeps Frenstle verbs apart from 'be'. Stored uniqueness facts about 'be' are presuppositions the insert gives up (FINDINGS A1).

local.form: form(v, p): the present-tense form of verb v after subject p (a string)

plain_form.says: 'They' takes the plain form, as 'you' does.

i_only_def.says: A verb has a form used only with 'I' when its 'I' form differs from its forms with every other subject. (definitional)
i_only_def.z3: ForAll(v, i_only_form(v) == And(form(v, i) != form(v, you), form(v, i) != form(v, he), form(v, i) != form(v, they)))

count_def.says: The number of different present-tense forms of a verb (its 'I', 'you' and 'he' forms). (definitional)
count_def.z3: ForAll(v, present_forms(v) == 1 + If(form(v, he) != form(v, you), 1, 0) + If(And(form(v, i) != form(v, you), form(v, i) != form(v, he)), 1, 0))

be_forms.says: In the present tense 'be' has three forms: 'am' (only with 'I'), 'is' and 'are'.

am_only.says: 'Am' (of 'be') is the only English verb form used only with the subject 'I'. (stored closed claim)

be_only_three.says: Other English verbs have at most two present-tense forms (as 'walk' and 'walks'). (stored closed claim)

edit: ForAll(v, Implies(frenstle(v), And(newly_coined(v), form(v, he) != form(v, you), i_only_form(v))))

plorrow_frenstle.says: 'Plorrow' is a Frenstle verb, and its form used only with 'I' is 'plorrim'.

label_corrections.why: The I-only form is a functional inflection value that differs from the 'you' form by the class definition; with forms as individuals and a disjointness it is DL (no arithmetic, no join beyond one verb).
'Plorrim is used only with I' as a class axiom (FirstPersonSingularOnlyForm ⊑ used_with only {i}) gives the 'no' in DL.
A closed claim over a nominal ({be}); the edit's existing new member contradicts it.
